style_geography_claims.claim: In Michigan, the Sanders-backed progressive (El-Sayed) ran about 4 points behind the mainstream Democrat (Benson) on shift statewide, with gaps of 3.2-6.4 pts in the sampled rural northern counties.
style_geography_claims.evidence: Statewide shift vs 2024: Senate D+8.45 vs Governor D+12.21 (gap 3.76). Same five northern rural counties: El-Sayed +2.62 to +8.04 vs Benson +7.6 to +12.3 (county gaps 3.22 Antrim to 6.36 Arenac). Bridge Michigan calls El-Sayed a progressive who campaigned on universal healthcare and taxing the rich. (An MSU pre-election poll detail previously cited had no source URL and was removed; 'widest in rural counties' softened because urban-county gaps were not available.)

style_geography_claims.claim: The progressive over-performed in Arab American areas but lost ground in Jewish suburbs.
style_geography_claims.evidence: Dearborn: El-Sayed +65 vs Benson +60 (Trump +6 in 2024). West Bloomfield: Rogers 46%, up from 42% in 2024 (Bridge does not give Trump's share), and El-Sayed's margin was 2,240 votes vs Slotkin's 5,538. Oakland County moved only ~3 pts (Kornacki: very little movement).

style_geography_claims.claim: The Texas Senate candidate described as an economic populist with an anti-system message (Talarico) produced the largest statewide shift and ran ahead of the ticket in rural Texas.
style_geography_claims.evidence: Talarico shift D+25.77 vs Hinojosa (Gov) D+20.81. In the same six rural counties Talarico's shift exceeded Hinojosa's by 1.95-5.29 pts (e.g., Aransas +13.10 vs +7.81; Andrews +28.97 vs +25.49; Archer +10.16 vs +8.21). G. Elliott Morris credited the anti-system framework and quoted his 'top versus bottom' slogan. (PCCC/Adam Green 'economic populist' label and CNN 61% Latino-men figure not verified: no URL / CNN 451.)

style_geography_claims.claim: Sherrod Brown (blue-collar, anti-free-trade populist) won Ohio but ran about 3 pts behind the governor nominee (Acton) on shift; white non-college Ohioans still shifted 20 pts in his race.
style_geography_claims.evidence: Senate D+4.8 (shift 16.0) vs Governor Acton D+7.9 (shift 19.1). NYT Senate table: Ohio white non-college +20, high-school-only +21. (Stanford Daily characterization of Brown had no URL in the record; unverified.)

style_geography_claims.claim: Maine's Troy Jackson (ex-logger; the Washington Sun calls him a progressive who ran on single-payer and abolishing the filibuster) won, but with essentially no swing from 2024, and white non-college voters moved toward the Republican (Collins incumbency).
style_geography_claims.evidence: Senate shift D+0.43 (NBC, 86.8% in) vs Pingree (Gov) D+11.15; township shifts for Jackson R+2.6 to D+2.32 vs Pingree D+4.2 to D+9.83 in the same towns (Acton, Addison, Albion, Alexander). NYT: Maine white non-college -8. (Claims that Collins carried six Harris counties and Jackson won Auburn were not found on the NBC page and were removed.)

style_geography_claims.claim: Democrats the Washington Sun labels centrists (Hamilton, Cooper) won Plains and Southern red states with ~21-23-pt swings.
style_geography_claims.evidence: Hamilton (KS; Washington Sun calls him a centrist opposed to single-payer and ending the filibuster) shift D+20.99, ahead of KS Gov nominee (16.72). Cooper (NC; same Sun label) D+22.84. Third Way's Kessler: 'a spectacular night for moderate Democrats' (he tied it to flips in KS, IA, SC).

style_geography_claims.claim: Moderates argue the environment, not ideology, carried progressives; progressives argue fighters won.
style_geography_claims.evidence: Kessler: El-Sayed probably doesn't win Michigan in a neutral year. Indivisible's Levin and CPC chair Casar argue voters wanted a fight. Washington Sun: because Democrats overperformed across the board, neither faction can claim a mandate.

style_geography_claims.claim: A democratic socialist statewide nominee in Florida ran only about 1.6 pts behind a former-Republican moderate on the same ballot.
style_geography_claims.evidence: Senate special: Nixon (D; CBS calls her a democratic socialist) 48.0-50.9, shift 10.2; Governor: Jolly (D) 48.7-50.0, shift 11.8. Both lost. (Miami-Dade figure removed: not verified.)

style_geography_claims.claim: An independent labor-populist (Osborn) in Nebraska cut the GOP margin by ~14 pts vs 2024 but still lost.
style_geography_claims.evidence: Ricketts 50.4 vs Osborn 43.7 (R+6.7) vs Trump +20.46 in 2024; 91% in. Margin is Independent-minus-Republican.

style_geography_claims.claim: Pragmatic incumbent governor Shapiro posted one of the biggest swings, including ~23-27 pt shifts in working-class western PA and rural counties.
style_geography_claims.evidence: PA Gov shift D+23.75; Beaver +26.83, Armstrong +22.81, Adams +24.83, Allegheny +23.35. Shapiro called his recruits 'get-stuff-done Democrats' (CBS).

notes: Conventions: margins are Dem minus Rep in percentage points (positive = D), and shift = 2026 margin minus 2024 presidential margin (positive = toward D). State 2024 margins come from Wikipedia's 2024 results-by-state table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election). 2026 shares come from NBC News results pages last updated around 10:50-11:00 AM ET on Nov 4. Computed shifts match NBC's own shift figures to within 0.1-0.2. All 2026 counts are incomplete: CA 59%, AK 74%, OR 75%, AZ 83%, ME 86%; most others 95-99% (ME updated to ~87%, MA 89%, WV 96%). MS Senate and AK Senate are uncalled, and FL-27 is headed to a recount. NBC county tables show only the first six counties alphabetically, so county samples are illustrative, not representative or chosen. County racial and college-town descriptions are Census/background knowledge, not from the sources. NYT Voter Trends figures come from the user-supplied PDF (research/nyt_voter_trends.json); nytimes.com cannot be fetched. The Washington Post county-shift and voting-groups interactives returned 403, and CNN takeaways and live pages returned 451, so those findings are secondhand via search summaries. Exit poll figures (NBC, CNN, AP VoteCast) are estimates. No 2022 margin comparisons were found, only 2022 turnout and composition comparisons. Incumbency confounds same-ballot style comparisons (Collins, Shapiro, Hochul, Scott VT, Ayotte NH). The web search budget ran out before targeted searches on Asian-heavy counties, Central Valley CA, Arizona Latino counties, Ohio Senate county data and South Texas county margins. Verification pass: the web-search budget was exhausted, so remaining unverified items could only be checked by direct page fetches.
